$Comment:
What Enchanting means at the lesser Disenchanting Table. It extends the jar's Disenchant action through the SCOPED target {Station: Disenchanting_Table, Action: Disenchant}, so it reaches that action on that one station and nowhere else. An extension's additions never flow down a Parent chain, so the greater table's own action (Disenchant_Greater, a child of Disenchant) never sees this file: DisenchantingGreaterProgression.json is a Parent child of this one that changes only its Target and its Bonus, so the two tables share one set of numbers and a retune here reaches both.

The jar owns the ritual, its presentation, its custody and its recipe; this pack owns what progression means at it, how long the ritual runs here, and how the Crafting and Enchanting trees' table techniques change the one Disenchant ritual for the player who holds them.

(1) PerCycleContributions. One cycle is one whole ritual (one piece unmade, 15 to 34 seconds here), so each amount is per piece, not per few seconds the way the Sawmill's are. ENCHANTING counts full and CRAFTING half, the station's own skill full and the adjacent one half. Both post on mmoskilltree:skill_xp (Param is the skill id), which the MMO bridge awards as skill XP.

(2) ContributionScale. The jar's Disenchant action authors none, so this one stands alone and multiplies the two amounts above before they are posted, from the piece on the table: item level at 1, quality at 5 per step, durability at a tenth per percent (a worn piece reads lower) and stamped enhancement points at a half each (an enhanced piece reads higher). The highest floor reached wins; below the first floor the scale is 1. A crude piece stays at 1, an iron piece reaches 1.25, the cobalt to adamantite band 1.5, a mithril piece 2 and an enhanced mithril piece 2.5. If the jar ever authors its own ContributionScale, remember that an extension's Factors and Floors each replace the action's whole array.

(3) Pace. The jar's own ritual is a short one, about 15 seconds untrained and down to about 3 with all the disenchanter's gear, so a server without this pack is not kept waiting. Here the ritual is the long one. Stretch 2.5 makes every paced beat two and a half times its jar length (Open 2 seconds, Kindle 8, Draw 12, Surge 9, Unmake 1.5, then the 1.5-second bloom: 34 seconds untrained). Clamp Min 0.42 narrows the jar action's range so a ritual never drops under 15 seconds; it binds before the stretch. A trained enchanter works faster as well as luckier: this ladder reads MMO_StationPace_ENCHANTING, Enchanting's main line (0.4 a point spent on the Enchanting tree, never a level, so a ritual speeds up as the points are spent), in steps of four points of the stat, each step four percent shorter, and its scale MULTIPLIES the jar action's proficiency ladder (softened back to its gentler curve here by DisenchantingProficiency.json). The whole tree spent (99 points, 39.6 of the stat, so that floor sits at 39.5 for the stat map's float rounding) brings the paced beats to 0.6 of their length (about 21 seconds a ritual); the full disenchanter's kit alone to about 19; both reach the 15-second floor. The floors past it are there for gear or a buff that carries the stat. The pace reaches the paced beats only (Open, Kindle, Draw, Surge, Unmake); the closing Payout beat keeps its 1.5 seconds.

(4) Bonus.Lootables names only the tables this pack ADDS: Mmo_Disenchant_Essence_Pay (more Life essence, sized by luck), Mmo_Disenchant_Salvage_Extras (now and then more of the salvage return's main material), Mmo_Disenchant_Void_Finds (luck-weighted Void essence), Mmo_Disenchant_Voidheart (the luck-weighted Voidheart) and Mmo_Disenchant_Voidheart_Base (the jar's own flat one, moved out of the jar's Disenchant_Void), Mmo_Disenchant_Talents and Mmo_Disenchant_Greater_Essence (what the Crafting and Enchanting trees' station stats pay here), and the two technique tables, Mmo_Disenchant_Rites (the wage paid again) and Mmo_Disenchant_Seekers (the finds rolled again). The pack also ships Disenchant_Essence.json, Disenchant_Void.json, Disenchant_Kit.json and DisenchantTrophy.json, which carry the ids of tables the jar's action already lists, so they replace the jar's versions in place; listing any of them here would roll it twice.

(5) The table techniques, as per-player settings on the one Disenchant ritual (never a second action, so a piece placed by anyone is unmade the way the player working it chose). Each reads the talent's own record (ziggfreedcommon:track_pick), and every setting is opt-in: it switches on only for a player its gate names, so a player without the talent, and a server with Crafting or Enchanting switched off or no such track at all, unmakes exactly as the jar authors:
- Quick Unmaking (Crafting, the Table Technique): StepOverlays skips the Draw beat for its holder (the ritual takes about two thirds of the time: 22 of 34 seconds untrained, 10 of 15 at the floor), and skips the Payout beat too, whose place the inserted Payout_Quick beat takes: the same bloom and length, rolling only Mmo_Disenchant_Quick_Return, so the ritual pays the return alone, with Table Practice bringing back the salvage extras and then the wage at half.
- Strip Down (Crafting, the Table Technique): Recipe.Fallback.CraftingShare.PreferWhen puts the crafting-share route ahead of the salvage rows for its holder, so a piece with a crafting recipe gives back a share of it instead of the bench's salvage (a piece whose recipe leaves no line still salvages); the share's Ladder makes it a third (Share 0.3 times 1.1), and Table Practice adds five points a rank (1.2667, 1.4333 of the jar's 0.3). Its holder's Payout is the inserted Payout_Strip beat, which rolls nothing, so no Essence or finds.
- Rite of Plenty (Enchanting, the Rite) and Essence Only (Enchanting, the Essence Trade): Recipe.Fallback.EssenceOnly.PreferWhen puts the essence-only route ahead of the salvage rows for either holder, so the piece gives back no salvage at all; their extra Essence of Life is Mmo_Disenchant_Rites. A player holding a preferred share and a preferred essence route takes the share, the first route in order.
- Treasure Hunter (Enchanting, the Seeker's Trade): Recipe.Yield.Ladder halves the salvage return for its holder (a line of one stays one, the engine's one-item floor), and Mmo_Disenchant_Seekers rolls each find again on half of all rituals.
- Void Rite and Kit Rite (Enchanting, the Seeker's Rite), with Seeker's Practice: gated rolls in Mmo_Disenchant_Seekers, and the Requires on Disenchant_Essence (Void Rite) and on the Void tables (Kit Rite).

Every number here is balance data and retunes by editing this one file.

Insert.$Comment: Quick Unmaking's payout, in place of the jar's Payout beat (which skips itself for this talent's holder): the same 1.5-second bloom at the piece's last place, rolling only what the technique keeps (Mmo_Disenchant_Quick_Return). It runs for the talent's holder alone; for everyone else its Conditions fail and it is skipped.

Strip Down's payout, in place of the jar's Payout beat (which skips itself for this talent's holder): the same 1.5-second bloom, rolling nothing, so the ritual pays its share of the piece's recipe and no Essence or finds. It runs for the talent's holder alone; for everyone else its Conditions fail and it is skipped.
